notes:
Cliopatria's British Africa is a composite of the British Empire's African holdings (the Wikipedia title is 'Scramble for Africa'), and its shapes carry four kinds of error that the pages opened show. (1) The Egyptian Sudan is inside the 1885-1889 shape although the Mahdist State held it from 1885 to 1898 (its Cliopatria 1890 shape coincides with these cells). (2) Asian lands are inside the 1917-1946 shapes: Palestine, Transjordan, Syria and Lebanon, Mesopotamia, Persia and Kuwait; they are British Empire holdings in Asia, not African, and British Colonial Empire (eu-11) carries a part of the same lands (Iraq 39 percent in 1919); they are cut out here and belong to the Middle East dossiers, with no ledger event. (3) Land that was not British direct rule is painted British: Darfur before 1916, the Lado Enclave (Congo Free State and Belgian Congo) before 10 June 1910, Barotseland before 1911, Matabeleland before 1894, the Boer republics before Vereeniging, northern Mozambique in 1918, the Belgian-occupied Ruanda-Urundi and Kigoma district in 1917-1921, South West Africa and German East Africa before their mandates, and Ethiopia, Eritrea, Italian Somaliland and Libya under British military administration (1941-1952; Somalia to 1959). Conquered and administered lands are therefore taken out of the keyframes and re-added as occupation events (hatched), and Egypt, a nominally independent client and then a protectorate, is taken out and added as vassal events. (4) A block of 1,837 cells in south-eastern Libya (the Libyan Desert around Kufra, 1905-1929, with 280 cells left to 1935) is in the shape; no page opened mentions it, so it stays as Cliopatria draws it and a gap-filler should check it.

Why the dossier runs 1885-1960 and has no capital: it is a composite of colonies ruled from London and from many local seats, so identity.capitals is empty; the map should draw no dot. The 1960 dissolve is a Cliopatria relabelling (British East Africa 1961-1972, Tanzania and Sierra Leone from 1961), not a historical event. Counterpart slugs: where a dossier by another group exists the slug is used (ndebele-kingdom, lozi-kingdom, sultanate-of-darfur, colony-of-natal, free-orange-state, south-african-republic, swaziland, kingdom-of-buganda, imperial-british-east-africa-company, mahdist-state); those groups use british-colonial-empire for the British side, this row uses british-africa.

Overlaps with dossiers other groups wrote or will write, to be settled by the orchestrator (rendering must not draw both): british-cape-colony (1795-1910, the whole Cape inside this row from 1885), colony-of-natal, orange-river-colony and transvaal-colony (1902-1910), whose successor union-of-south-africa has no dossier (this row holds the Union 1910-1931; Cliopatria's South Africa row starts in 1932); basutoland (Lesotho, in every shape from 1885), sierra-leone-colony-and-protectorate (Sierra Leone) and the Gambia, british-bechuanaland (1885-1895), swaziland, mahdist-state (whose successor slug anglo-egyptian-sudan has no dossier: the Sudan 1899-1955 is inside this row; mahdist-state dates Dongola September 1896, Abu Hamed 7 August 1897, Omdurman 2 September 1898 and the remnant's end in November 1899, which this dossier did not open pages for), turco-egyptian-sudan, kingdom-of-egypt (1922-1952), south-africa (1932-), british-gold-coast (which already holds Nigeria, the Gold Coast and the Cameroons, so those are absent here), italian-africa and german-africa (the counterparts of the occupations), belgian-congo (Lado, Kigoma, Ruanda-Urundi), lozi-kingdom (to 1911) and british-east-africa (1961-1972).

Counterparts that need dossiers: sultanate-of-egypt (1914-1922 protectorate; slug sultanate-of-egypt) and an extension of khedivate-of-egypt to 1914 (the Cliopatria row stops in 1884; this row holds Egypt as a client from 1885), anglo-egyptian-sudan, union-of-south-africa (1910-1931 or 1961), and the British Military Administrations of Eritrea, Italian Somaliland, Ethiopia and Libya as occupations. Names the gazetteer lacks: 'Lado Enclave' (Central Equatoria stands in for it, about 23,000 km2 against the page's 39,000 km2).

Not settled for lack of pages (page budget): the Bechuanaland, Basutoland, Sierra Leone and Gambia holdings (no page opened mentions them); Matabeleland's year (page silent; 1894 comes from the ndebele-kingdom dossier); the Libyan Desert block; Sinai in 1915-1917; Jubaland (no page); Swaziland's 1908 transfer; Nyasaland's extent; the status of Italian Somaliland after 1950 (the shape keeps it British to 1959); the 1941 dates of Mogadishu, Addis Ababa and Massawa and the January 1942 Anglo-Ethiopian agreement (the East African campaign page is silent); the Allied occupation of Libya 1943-1951 (the Kingdom of Libya page is silent); Zanzibar and Pemba (a British protectorate from 1890 per the Scramble page; only 18 Tanzania cells are in the shape before 1916); Fashoda and Omdurman dates (silent on the pages opened); the Suez Canal Zone and British forces in Egypt after 1922 (not on the Sultanate page). Disagreements inside pages: British Somaliland is a protectorate from 1884 and established in 1888; recaptured in March or on 8 April 1941; the Sudan page gives self-rule as 22 October 1952 in the infobox and March 1953 in the text; the Union page says South West Africa was both annexed and never formally annexed. The Lado Enclave page was opened for the belgian-congo dossier and cited here as a fifteenth page. fx-25 (2026-11-01): from 1911 the keyframes no longer draw the Union of South Africa (own dossier south-africa; ledger loss 31 May 1910) and the 1911-1919 keyframes leave out the interior of British Somaliland that the Dervish state held (ledger loss 1910, gain February 1920). fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the keyframes of 1905-1932 no longer draw Libya except the Sarra Triangle (the Cliopatria shape held about 1,940 Libyan cells); the p1920-p1929 Kufra ruling for senussi-order against this state is then redundant.
